ops.text: capt-hook comment-budget guard blocks cleaning up STALE comments inside pre-existing over-budget comment blocks. During the secrets.sh→`yclaw secret reconcile` cleanup, five scripts (bootstrap.sh:3,23-24, redeploy.sh:17, bluebubbles-setup.sh:32, nuke-tailnet.sh:8, plus the scope-fenced container-vault.sh:27) carry now-stale references to the deleted `secrets.sh`/`collect_secrets`/`_ts_mint_key`/`cliproxy_key_from_metal_bundle` inside multi-line header/inline comment blocks that ALREADY exceeded the repo's comment-length guard (3-line/200-char plain) before the edit. The guard flags any edit that touches part of an already-over-budget contiguous block — not just the delta — so even progressively-shorter single-line replacements are rejected (verified across 3 rounds by the cleanup agent). Net effect: you cannot delete or shorten a stale line without rewriting the entire surrounding 5-17 line architectural comment, which is disproportionate for a mechanical repoint. These references are comment-only (zero functional code references the deleted helpers — verified), so left as documented debt. Ask: exempt pure deletions/shrinks from the budget check (an edit whose result is <= the block's prior length should always pass), or scope the check to the changed hunk rather than the enclosing block.
